name: John Ellerton
bio: John Ellerton (1826–1893) was an English hymn-writer and hymnologist.

The poems here are taken from Alfred H. Miles (ed.), The Poets and the Poetry of the Century (London: Hutchinson, 1891–1897), vol. 10, from the Internet Archive scans of that edition. Spelling is that of the anthology; Miles's biographical essay and extracts from longer poems are omitted, and only poems that could be read cleanly from the scan are included.

poems.title: Throned upon the Awful Tree
poems.author: John Ellerton
poems.text:
Throned upon the awful Tree,
King of grief, I watch with Thee
Darkness veils Thine anguished face.
None its lines of woe can trace, i
None can tell what pangs unknown
Hold Thee silent and alone.

Silent through those three dread hours
Wrestling with the evil powers;
Left alone with human sin,
Gloom around Thee and within,
Till the appointed time is nigh.
Till the Lamb of God may die.

Hark that cry that peals aloud
Upward through the whelming cloud
Thou, the Father's only Son,
Thou, His own Anointed One,
Thou dost ask Him— can it be?
"Why hast Thou forsaken Me?

Lord, should fear and anguish roll
Darkly o'er my' sinful soul.
Thou, who once wast thus bereft
That Thine own might ne'er be left —
Teach me by that bitter cry
In the gloom to know Thee nigh.

poems.title: The day Thou gavest, Lord, is ended
poems.author: John Ellerton
poems.text:
The day Thou gavest, Lord, is ended;
The darkness falls at Thy behest;
To Thee our morning hymns ascended,
Thy praise shall sanctify our rest.

We thank Thee that Thy Church unsleeping,
While earth rolls onward into light,
Through all the world her watch is keeping,
And rests not now by day or night.

As o'er each continent and island
The Dawn leads on another day.
The voice of prayer is never silent.
Nor dies the strain of praise away".

The sun that bids us rest is waking
Our brethren 'neath the Western sky,
And hour by hour fresh lips are making
Thy wondrous doings heard on high.

So be it, Lord; Thy throne shall never,
Like earth's proud empires, pass away;
Thy kingdom stands, and grows for ever.
Till all Thy creatures own Thy sway.

poems.title: Saviour, again to Thy dear name we raise
poems.author: John Ellerton
